s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ocular and musculoskeletal abnormalities with onset in adolescence
salient_findings: Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
key_facts: Age of onset of elevated intraocular pressure: 13 years
Patient's height: 180.4 cm
Presence of long fingers
Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
Family history of similar findings: negative
Serial echocardiograms: no abnormalities
Open iridocorneal angle in each eye
No evidence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
Subtle lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye first observed at age 17
Lens dislocation in the left eye developed at age 32
Genetic testing revealed 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene

shortlist.label: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by ectopia lentis, glaucoma, and short stature, but can also present with tall stature and joint hypermobility

shortlist.label: Homocystinuria
shortlist.why_kept: Causes ectopia lentis, glaucoma, and tall stature with joint hypermobility due to homocysteine accumulation

shortlist.label: Marfan syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Features tall stature, ectopia lentis, and joint hypermobility, although aortic root dilatation is commonly seen and not present in this case

shortlist.label: LTBP2-related ocular syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing revealed 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, which is associated with glaucoma and lens dislocation

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by joint hypermobility and can have ocular features such as ectopia lentis, although not as prominent as in other conditions

raw.rationale: The patient's genetic testing revealed 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, which is a strong indicator of LTBP2-related ocular syndrome. The presence of elevated intraocular pressure, lens dislocation, and optic nerve cupping also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's tall stature and absence of short fingers do not align with Weill-Marchesani syndrome

rejected.label: Homocystinuria
rejected.why: There is no mention of intellectual disability, thromboembolism, or other systemic features typical of homocystinuria

rejected.label: Marfan syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's normal serial echocardiograms and lack of other systemic features such as aortic root dilatation do not support Marfan syndrome

rejected.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has hypermobility, the primary features of elevated intraocular pressure and lens dislocation are more specific to LTBP2-related ocular syndrome
